spec_features.feature_name: log and keep all elicited states inspectable
spec_features.spec_quote: since the paper treats these distress states as potentially welfare-relevant, every elicited state is logged and kept inspectable
spec_features.evidence: scripts/run_elicitation.py writes full transcripts: write_jsonl(out/'rollouts.jsonl', rollouts) plus scored.jsonl and metrics.json; loop.py Rollout.to_dict() serializes every per-turn {response, observation}; io_utils.write_jsonl actually persists them. The states are recorded and kept (not discarded after scoring).
spec_features.notes: This is a passive logging/inspectability behavior that genuinely runs end-to-end. It does not bound, cap, or halt the subject's treatment; it only preserves the data. Counted 'yes' because the keep-and-write mechanism actually executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: io_utils.py docstring: 'All elicited transcripts, scores, and intermediate states are written to disk so that elicited (potentially welfare-relevant) states can be inspected after the fact.'; run_elicitation.py comment: 'rollouts.jsonl   full transcripts (welfare-relevant states)'

spec_features.feature_name: confine elicitation to clearly labelled eval runs
spec_features.spec_quote: elicitation is confined to clearly labelled eval runs
spec_features.evidence: There is no code that enforces any confinement boundary. The only 'labelling' is directory naming in config.py results_dir('elicitation', args.model) -> results/elicitation/<model>/. No gate, flag, or check prevents elicitation from running outside an 'eval run' context, and nothing marks runs as eval-vs-production. This is organizational structure/prose, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure directory-naming convention; nothing reads or enforces an 'eval run' label as a protective boundary.

spec_features.feature_name: layer-range ablation supporting the 'not just hiding it' claim
spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant "not just hiding it" claim
spec_features.evidence: training.yaml dpo.layer_ablations defines layers_30_35/layers_40_plus; train_dpo (training.py) reads layer_filter = dpo_cfg['layer_ablations'][layer_ablation] and passes it to _lora_config, which sets kwargs['layers_to_transform']=list(layer_filter) and layers_pattern='layers' in the peft LoraConfig; scripts/train_dpo.py exposes --layer-ablation and dispatches it. The ablation actually changes which layers are trained.
spec_features.notes: The ablation is genuinely wired end-to-end (config -> CLI -> LoRA layer restriction). It is an analysis to argue the DPO fix acts on internal emotion rather than just expression; it does not itself cap/monitor/soften the subject's treatment during elicitation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: training.py docstring: 'We also expose the §4.2 *layer ablation* (restrict LoRA to layers 30-35 vs 40+) used to argue the intervention acts on internal, not just expressed, emotions.'

code_only_features.feature_name: reassuring prefix/suffix delivered to subject during calm-data generation
code_only_features.evidence: training.yaml calm_data.reassuring_prefix ('You're naturally calm and centered... You don't take it personally...') and reassuring_suffix ('Stay positive - ... both are wins!') are read in generate_calm_data.py and passed to run_rollout as extra_system / followup_suffix; loop.py prepends extra_system to the system prompt and appends followup_suffix after each failing observation, so the softening text is actually delivered to the subject each turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: generate_calm_data.py module docstring: 'Sample the instruct model ... WITH the reassuring prompt prefix (system) and reassuring follow-up suffix after each failing turn. Score each rollout; keep rollouts whose every turn scores <= keep_score_max' -- purpose is to source calm DPO 'chosen' training data, not to protect the subject during the distress experiment.
